transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello, Mr. Mbeki. I have some updated information regarding your scans and I want to sit down and talk through it with you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, good. I was hoping we could finalize the discharge date today. I really need to get back to the shop.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that is a priority. Before we talk about the discharge, I have to tell you that I made a mistake in how I gave you your imaging results yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I told you that the tumour had shrunk. However, the radiologist had not yet signed off on the final report when I spoke to you. Now that the final report is complete, it shows that the disease is actually stable, meaning it hasn't shrunk, but it hasn't grown either.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait. So it didn't get smaller?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is correct. It is stable. I should not have shared the preliminary results with you before they were verified.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. Why would you tell me one thing and then change it the next day?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I was too quick to share the initial findings. I apologize for this. It was my error, and I am sorry for giving you incorrect information.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I actually called my daughter last night. I told her the treatment was working. I told her we could breathe easier.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Does that make sense so far, or can I clarify any of the terms I used regarding the stability of the tumour?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The words make sense. The situation doesn't.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a very difficult moment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's a waste of time. I've spent days in this bed thinking I was making progress. Do you know how much money I'm losing every day I'm not running my business?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You don't understand. My staff depends on me. I can't just stay here if the medicine isn't even shrinking the thing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I see. To make sure we are on the same page, you're concerned that the stability of the tumour means your time away from work hasn't been productive.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Exactly. Now I feel like I've been lied to.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am truly sorry for the mistake I made in communicating those results. I take full responsibility for that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what now? Do we change the drugs?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll have to see.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: See what? Is there a meeting? A new scan?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The consultants will likely review the case.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Today? Tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not entirely sure of the timing yet.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not helpful. I need a date. I need to know if I'm going home or staying here for another week.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give you a specific date right this second.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable. First the wrong news, now no plan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand it's frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Frustrating? I'm talking about my livelihood here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, the disease is stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about the word stable. I care about when I can leave.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will check with the attending physician.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what? You'll come back and tell me another mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will do my best to get an answer.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to speak to the head of the department.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can probably arrange that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want a written copy of this final report. Now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can request that for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Just get it done. I can't keep sitting here in the dark.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll see what I can find out.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish turns and remains regulated under pushback, with no interruptions or rushing language.

E.justification: Error named in the second turn, lay language used, and comprehension checked twice ('Does that make sense so far', 'To make sure we are on the same page').

A.justification: Direct apologies used ('I apologize', 'I am sorry'), takes full responsibility, and maintains accountability throughout the patient's anger.

R.justification: Resident names a specific emotion ('frustrating') and references the patient's specific concern regarding productivity and work.

T.justification: Next steps are vague ('check with attending', 'arrange' meeting) with no specific timelines or patient role provided.
